legend: PET identified extensive 68Ga-DOTATATE reactivity involving the sella, extending into the suprasellar space and inferiorly to the posterior fossa and upper cervical spine (short arrow). Multiple intrathecal deposits in the mid-cervical and upper thoracic spine are also noted, with abnormal radiotracer uptake in the hilar, mediastinal, periportal, and retroperitoneal nodes (long arrows).

A PitNET with both extensive cerebrospinal fluid dissemination and focal brain invasion. The tumour cells are relatively homogeneous and there is a pseudorosette around a vascular channel. Note the mitosis (arrow).
A PitNET with both extensive cerebrospinal fluid dissemination and focal brain invasion. The tumour invades into surrounding brain parenchyma.
A PitNET with both extensive cerebrospinal fluid dissemination and focal brain invasion. A smear preparation shows cellular homogeneity but identifies a mitosis (arrow).
Immunohistochemical features of the metastatic PitNET. The tumour shows diffuse synaptophysin positivity.
Immunohistochemical features of the metastatic PitNET. The tumour cells are negative for all pituitary hormones and cytokeratins (shown here).
Immunohistochemical features of the metastatic PitNET. GFAP highlights reactive astrocytes in the region of brain invasion. The Ki-67 labelling index of this tumour was very high.
Immunohistochemical features of the metastatic PitNET. The Ki-67 labelling index of this tumour is very high.
Metastatic corticotroph PitNET to bone. The presence of tumour invading bone confirms the diagnosis.
Metastatic corticotroph PitNET to bone. The invading tumour cells are positive for ACTH.
Metastatic corticotroph PitNET to bone. The metastatic tumour stains intensely for keratins using the CAM5.2 antibody.
The metastatic tumour cells are mainly large and pleomorphic. Nuclei are atypical. Some cells (arrow) demonstrate the appearance of Crooke cells.

legend: Crooke cell subtype. Many tumour cells show positive granular staining for ACTH in the cytoplasm. Some tumour cells (arrow) demonstrate Crooke cell change.

legend: Crooke cell subtype. Many tumour cells show strong and ring-like staining for keratin (CAM5.2). Some cells (arrow) exhibit a Crooke cell appearance.
source: The figure is courtesy of Dr.Shigeyuki Tahara and Dr.Ryuji Ohashi, Nippon Medical School Tokyo

legend: Crooke cell subtype, liver metastasis. This figure shows the mixture of pleomorphic tumour cells (single asterisk) and admixed hepatocytes (double asterisk).
